exercises.name: Snatch
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, quads, hamstrings, traps, shoulders, upper back
instructions: Set the feet about hip width with toes turned out, take a wide grip, and start with the bar over the balls of the feet and the shoulders above the bar.
Push through the whole foot and keep the same back angle until the bar passes the knees.
Extend the hips and legs hard while the bar stays close to the body.
Pull the elbows up and out, move the feet to your squat stance, and drop under the bar.
Lock the bar overhead in a full squat, then stand up under control.
exercises.formCue: Bar close, finish tall, punch up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending the arms early, or letting the bar swing away from the body.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start with a dowel or empty bar and learn the power snatch from the hang first.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the first competition lift and trains speed, power, and mobility in one movement.

exercises.name: Power Snatch
instructions: Set up as for the snatch with a wide grip, the bar over the balls of the feet, and the shoulders above the bar.
Push through the whole foot and hold your back angle until the bar passes the knees.
Extend the hips hard with the bar close, then pull the elbows up and out.
Move the feet out and receive the bar locked out overhead in a partial squat with the thighs above parallel.
Stand up under control.
exercises.formCue: Finish the pull, then punch and stop high.
exercises.commonMistakes: Cutting the leg drive short to rush under the bar, or pressing the bar out with soft elbows.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a dowel or empty bar from the hang at mid-thigh.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Catching high demands a strong, fast pull and is easier to learn than the full snatch.

exercises.name: Hang Snatch
instructions: Deadlift the bar to standing with a snatch grip.
Lower it under control to the hang position you are training, balanced over the whole foot.
Push through the floor, then extend the hips hard with the bar close to the body.
Pull the elbows up and out, move the feet, and drop into a full squat under the bar.
Lock the bar overhead firmly and stand.
exercises.formCue: Shoulders over the bar, then finish tall.
exercises.commonMistakes: Swinging the bar out from the hips, or pulling with the arms before the legs finish.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the hang power snatch with an empty bar.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Starting from the hang isolates the final extension and the pull under the bar.

exercises.name: Hang Power Snatch
instructions: Deadlift the bar to standing with a snatch grip.
Lower it under control to the hang position, with the shoulders over the bar.
Push through the floor and extend the hips hard.
Pull the elbows up and out and receive the bar locked out overhead above a parallel squat.
Stand up and lower the bar under control.
exercises.formCue: Legs first, arms last.
exercises.commonMistakes: Using the arms to lift the bar, or catching with bent elbows.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practice with a dowel, starting from mid-thigh.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the simplest way to learn the snatch extension and overhead catch.

exercises.name: Muscle Snatch
instructions: Start as for the snatch and push through the whole foot until the bar is above the knees.
Extend the hips with the bar close, then shrug and pull the elbows up and out.
Keep the legs straight and turn the bar over as the elbows reach shoulder height.
Punch straight up to lockout with the bar over the back of the neck.
exercises.formCue: Elbows high, then turn it over and punch.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dropping the elbows before the turnover, or bending the knees again to get under the bar.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a dowel or empty bar and start from the hang.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches and strengthens the upper-body turnover of the snatch.

exercises.name: Tall Snatch
instructions: Stand tall with a snatch grip, the bar at arm's length, and the feet in your pulling stance.
Lift the feet and pull the elbows up and out at the same moment.
Turn the bar over and punch up as you drop into a squat, aiming to lock out as the feet land.
Hold the bottom with the bar secure overhead, then stand.
exercises.formCue: Pull yourself down, fast.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dipping the knees or leaning to get the bar moving first, or pressing the bar out slowly.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a PVC pipe and receive in a partial squat.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It isolates the pull under the bar and builds speed and confidence in the catch.

exercises.name: Block Snatch
instructions: Set the bar on blocks and take the same position you would pass through in a snatch at that height.
Balance over the whole foot, then push hard with the legs with the bar close.
Extend the hips fully once the bar passes the knees.
Pull the elbows up and out, move the feet, and receive the bar overhead in a squat.
Stand, then return the bar to the blocks.
exercises.formCue: Set your position, then go.
exercises.commonMistakes: Starting with the shoulders behind the bar, or rushing the pull because there is no run-up.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the hang snatch from the same height with a lighter load.
exercises.whyThisMatters: With no stretch or momentum to help, it builds a fast, strong start from a fixed position.

exercises.name: Snatch Pull
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, quads, traps, upper back
instructions: Set the snatch start position with the heels about hip width, the bar over the balls of the feet, and the shoulders above the bar.
Push through the whole foot and keep the bar close to the legs past the knees.
Open the hips and drive up with the legs as hard as you can.
Shrug and let the elbows bend slightly to keep the bar against the body, then return it to the floor.
exercises.formCue: Legs all the way, bar against the body.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pulling with the arms early, or letting the bar drift away from the body at the top.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start with the snatch deadlift to learn the positions at slow speed.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the strength and timing of the snatch extension with loads at or above the full lift.

exercises.name: Snatch High Pull
exercises.musclesWorked: Traps, upper back, shoulders, glutes, hamstrings
instructions: Set the snatch start position and push with the legs through the whole foot.
Keep the bar close until mid-thigh, then open the hips and drive up hard.
After the legs finish, shrug and pull the elbows up and out with the bar against the body.
Stay tall with the trunk vertical at the top, then lower the bar.
exercises.formCue: Elbows up and out, stay tall.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning forward to meet the bar, or pulling with the arms before the legs finish.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a light bar from the hang at mid-thigh.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It links the leg drive to the arm action that starts the pull under the bar.

exercises.name: Snatch Deadlift
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, quads, upper back, grip
instructions: Take a snatch-width grip with the heels about hip width, the bar over the balls of the feet, and the shoulders above the bar.
Set the back flat and push through the whole foot.
Keep the bar close and hold the same back angle until the bar reaches the thigh.
Extend the hips to stand tall, then lower the bar.
exercises.formCue: Same back angle to the knees.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the hips rise faster than the shoulders, or losing the flat upper back with the wide grip.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use straps and a lighter load, or pull from low blocks.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds strength and posture in the exact positions of the snatch pull.

exercises.name: Overhead Squat
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, shoulders, upper back, trunk
instructions: Hold the bar overhead with a snatch grip, elbows locked, shoulder blades squeezed together, and the bar over the base of the neck.
Set the feet in your squat stance and brace the trunk.
Squat to full depth at a controlled speed, balanced over the whole foot.
Keep pushing up into the bar as you stand.
exercises.formCue: Push up on the bar the whole time.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the bar drift forward of the base of the neck, or the elbows softening at the bottom.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the PVC overhead squat and only go as deep as you can hold the bar in place.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the strength, balance, and mobility needed to receive a snatch.

exercises.name: PVC Overhead Squat
instructions: Hold a PVC pipe overhead with a wide grip and locked elbows, over the base of the neck.
Squeeze the shoulder blades together and set your squat stance.
Squat slowly as deep as you can while the pipe stays in place and the weight stays over the whole foot.
Push up into the pipe and stand.
exercises.formCue: Reach up into the pipe as you sit.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the pipe drift forward, or rising onto the toes.
exercises.beginnerModification: Squat to a box, or widen the grip until the position holds.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Daily practice with no load is the simplest way to build the snatch receiving position.

exercises.name: Snatch Balance
instructions: Stand with the bar behind the neck, a snatch grip, the shoulder blades set tight, and the feet in your pulling stance.
Dip at the knees with the trunk upright and drive up just enough to unweight the bar.
Punch the arms up hard as you move the feet out and drop into an overhead squat.
Hold the bottom until the bar is steady, then stand.
exercises.formCue: Punch under, do not push the bar up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Driving the bar high and pressing it out, instead of moving fast under it.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the pressing snatch balance with an empty bar.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds speed, timing, and confidence for the catch of the snatch.

exercises.name: Pressing Snatch Balance
instructions: Stand with the bar behind the neck, a snatch grip, and the feet in your squat stance.
Start pressing the bar and squatting down at the same time, at a controlled speed.
Time it so the elbows lock just as you reach the bottom of the squat.
Make sure the bar is steady overhead, then stand.
exercises.formCue: Press yourself down under the bar.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pressing the bar up first and then squatting, or stopping short of full depth.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a PVC pipe and squat only as deep as you can keep the bar over the base of the neck.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the receiving position and overhead mobility at slow speed.

exercises.name: Snatch Push Press
instructions: Stand with the bar behind the neck, a snatch grip, and the shoulder blades set tight.
Dip at the knees with the trunk upright and drive hard through the floor.
As the bar leaves the shoulders, press fast into a firm lockout.
Hold a moment overhead, then lower the bar to the shoulders and reset.
exercises.formCue: Dip straight, drive, lock it hard.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning forward in the dip, or finishing with soft elbows.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use an empty bar or PVC pipe.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds the overhead strength and stability that holds a snatch in place.

exercises.name: Press in Snatch
instructions: With a snatch grip and the bar behind the neck, sit into the bottom of a squat.
Press the bar to full lockout without any help from the legs.
Keep the shoulder blades squeezed and the chest up while the bar is overhead.
Lower the bar under control to the upper back and repeat.
exercises.formCue: Stay down, chest up, press.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rising out of the squat to help the press, or letting the bar drop onto the neck.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a PVC pipe, or do the pressing snatch balance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds mobility, stability, and strength in the snatch receiving position.

exercises.name: PVC Pass-Through
instructions: Hold a PVC pipe in front of the hips with a wide overhand grip and straight arms.
Raise the pipe in a wide arc up and over the head without bending the elbows.
Continue the arc until the pipe rests behind the hips, then bring it back the same way.
Narrow the grip a little at a time only while the movement stays smooth and comfortable.
exercises.formCue: Arms long, slow arc.
exercises.commonMistakes: Bending the elbows to get through, or forcing a grip that is too narrow.
exercises.beginnerModification: Take a wider grip, or use a band so the hands can move apart.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It warms up the shoulders for the snatch and every overhead position.

exercises.name: Clean
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, quads, hamstrings, traps, upper back
instructions: Set the feet about hip width with toes turned out, grip just outside the legs, and start with the bar over the balls of the feet.
Push through the whole foot and hold your back angle until the bar passes the knees.
Extend the hips hard with the bar close, brushing the upper thigh.
Pull the elbows up, move the feet out, and whip the elbows around to rack the bar on the shoulders in a full squat.
Drive straight up out of the squat and stand.
exercises.formCue: Bar close, fast elbows.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the bar crash onto the shoulders with slow elbows, or jumping forward to chase a bar that swung out.
exercises.beginnerModification: Learn the hang power clean first, then add the front squat.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the first half of the clean and jerk and builds total-body power.

exercises.name: Power Clean
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, quads, traps, upper back
instructions: Set up with the feet about hip width, the bar over the balls of the feet, the shoulders above the bar, and the back flat.
Push through the whole foot and hold your back angle until the bar passes the knees.
Extend the hips hard with the bar close to the body.
Pull the elbows up, move the feet out, and whip the elbows around to rack the bar with the thighs above parallel.
Stand up fully.
exercises.formCue: Finish the legs, then fast elbows.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pulling with the arms early, or catching with the elbows low and the bar in the hands.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the hang power clean with an empty bar.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the most widely used lift for building power from the floor.

exercises.name: Hang Clean
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, quads, traps, upper back
instructions: Deadlift the bar to standing with a clean grip.
Lower it under control to the hang position you are training, balanced over the whole foot.
Push with the legs, then extend the hips hard with the bar close.
Pull the elbows up, move the feet, and rack the bar on the shoulders as you sit into a full squat.
Drive up out of the bottom right away and stand.
exercises.formCue: Extend, then pull under and sit.
exercises.commonMistakes: Catching high and then riding the bar down, instead of pulling under into the squat.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the hang power clean followed by a separate front squat.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Starting from the hang trains the final extension and a fast pull under the bar.

exercises.name: Muscle Clean
instructions: Start as for the clean and push through the whole foot until the bar is above the knees.
Extend the hips with the bar close to the body.
Keep the legs straight and pushing into the floor as you shrug and pull the elbows up and out.
Bring the elbows around and set the bar smoothly on the shoulders without bending the knees again.
exercises.formCue: Elbows high, then around.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dipping under the bar, or letting the bar loop away from the body.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use an empty bar from the hang.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches the arm path of the clean turnover and strengthens it.

exercises.name: Tall Clean
instructions: Stand tall with a clean grip, the bar at arm's length, and the feet in your pulling stance.
Lift the feet and pull the elbows up and out at the same moment.
Bring the elbows around fast and rack the bar as you drop into a squat.
Sit into the bottom smoothly, then stand right away.
exercises.formCue: Pull down and whip the elbows.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dipping or swinging the bar to start it moving, or receiving with the elbows low.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use an empty bar and receive in a partial squat.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It isolates the pull under the bar and builds a quick, precise turnover.

exercises.name: Block Clean
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, quads, traps, upper back
instructions: Set the bar on blocks and take the same position you would pass through in a clean at that height.
Push through the floor and hold your back angle until the bar passes the knees.
Extend the hips hard with the bar close, brushing the upper thigh.
Pull the elbows high, move into your squat stance, and whip the elbows around to rack the bar.
Drive up out of the squat, then return the bar to the blocks.
exercises.formCue: Tight start, full finish.
exercises.commonMistakes: Starting loose because the bar is already raised, or cutting the extension short.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the hang clean from the same height with a lighter load.
exercises.whyThisMatters: With no momentum from the floor, it builds speed and force in the top of the pull.

exercises.name: Clean Pull
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, hamstrings, quads, traps, spinal erectors
instructions: Set the clean start position with the heels about hip width, the bar over the balls of the feet, the shoulders above the bar, and the back flat.
Push through the whole foot and keep the bar close with the same back angle past the knees.
At mid-thigh, open the hips and drive up as hard as you can.
Shrug with slightly bent elbows to keep the bar tight to the body, then return to flat feet as the bar comes down.
exercises.formCue: Push the floor, finish tall, shrug.
exercises.commonMistakes: Yanking the bar off the floor, or bending the arms before the legs have finished.
exercises.beginnerModification: Start with the clean deadlift to learn the positions slowly.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It builds pulling strength and timing for the clean with loads at or above the full lift.

exercises.name: Clean Deadlift
instructions: Set the clean start position with the heels about hip width, the bar over the balls of the feet, and the shoulders above the bar.
Push through the whole foot with the chest up and the bar close to the legs.
Hold the same back angle until the bar passes the knees.
Extend the hips and legs to stand tall, then lower the bar under control.
exercises.formCue: Chest up, knees back, bar close.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the hips shoot up first, or pulling it like a powerlifting deadlift with the shoulders behind the bar.
exercises.beginnerModification: Pull from low blocks with a light load until the start position is comfortable.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the exact posture and bar path of the first part of the clean.

exercises.name: Clean and Jerk
exercises.musclesWorked: Glutes, quads, hamstrings, traps, shoulders, triceps
instructions: Clean the bar from the floor to the shoulders and stand up fully.
Reset the grip and breath, with the bar resting on the shoulders and the trunk upright.
Dip by bending only the knees, a short distance, then drive straight up hard.
Punch the bar overhead as the feet move into a split and the elbows lock.
Hold the bar steady, bring the feet back in line, and then lower it.
exercises.formCue: Stand tall, reset, then dip and drive straight.
exercises.commonMistakes: Rushing the jerk before the clean is settled, or dipping forward onto the toes.
exercises.beginnerModification: Train the power clean and push press as separate lifts first.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It is the second competition lift and puts the most weight overhead of any movement.

exercises.name: Split Jerk
exercises.musclesWorked: Quads, glutes, shoulders, triceps, upper back
instructions: Stand with the heels about hip width and the bar racked on the shoulders, elbows down and slightly in front of the bar.
Dip by bending only the knees with the trunk vertical, a short distance, and brake hard.
Drive straight up with the legs and push the bar up and slightly back.
Move the feet quickly into a split as you punch the elbows to lockout.
Hold the bar steady, then step the front foot back and the rear foot in.
exercises.formCue: Dip straight, drive, punch and split.
exercises.commonMistakes: Dipping forward so the bar goes out front, or a short, narrow split that leaves no base.
exercises.beginnerModification: Practice the footwork with a PVC pipe, then use the jerk balance.
exercises.whyThisMatters: The split gives the widest base for receiving heavy weights overhead.

exercises.name: Push Jerk
instructions: Rack the bar between the throat and the top of the shoulders, with the elbows slightly in front of the bar.
Dip by bending only the knees with the trunk vertical, then drive up hard.
As the legs finish, push the bar up and slightly back and punch the elbows to lockout.
Bend the knees again to receive the bar in a partial squat with the feet staying on the floor, then stand.
exercises.formCue: Drive, then push yourself under.
exercises.commonMistakes: Pressing the bar out slowly instead of dropping under it, or dipping with the chest forward.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the push press until the dip and drive are consistent.
exercises.whyThisMatters: Feet that stay planted teach a balanced, complete leg drive.

exercises.name: Power Jerk
instructions: Stand with the heels about hip width and the bar racked on the shoulders, elbows down and slightly forward.
Dip by bending only the knees with the trunk vertical, and brake hard.
Drive up hard with the legs and push the bar overhead.
Move the feet quickly out to your squat stance and punch the elbows to lockout in a partial squat.
Steady the bar, then stand.
exercises.formCue: Straight dip, hard drive, fast feet.
exercises.commonMistakes: Jumping forward or back, or catching with soft elbows.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use the push jerk, where the feet stay on the floor.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It demands a high, straight drive and is a simple way to train the jerk.

exercises.name: Jerk Dip Squat
instructions: Stand in your jerk stance with the bar in the jerk rack position and brace as you would for a jerk.
Dip by bending the knees at a controlled speed with the trunk upright.
Keep tension in the legs and stay balanced over the whole foot.
Change direction smoothly and stand back up without an explosive drive.
exercises.formCue: Straight down, straight up.
exercises.commonMistakes: Letting the chest tip forward, or the weight shifting to the toes.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use an empty bar and hold a short pause at the bottom of the dip.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It strengthens the dip position so the bar travels straight in the jerk.

exercises.name: Jerk Balance
exercises.equipment: Barbell or PVC pipe, squat rack
instructions: Rack the bar on the shoulders and stand in a short split, about one foot-length shorter than your full split.
Balance the weight evenly between both feet.
Dip straight down and drive straight up.
Step the front foot forward into the full split as you punch the bar to lockout, keeping the trunk upright.
Steady the bar, then recover the feet.
exercises.formCue: Step through, do not dive the chest.
exercises.commonMistakes: Leaning the chest forward, or putting most of the weight on the front leg.
exercises.beginnerModification: Use a PVC pipe or empty bar.
exercises.whyThisMatters: It teaches you to move under the bar into a balanced split.
